errors.statement: A doctorate lowers the predicted chance a great deal, and even more so if the occupation is handlers or cleaners: from about 84% to about 5% for handlers or cleaners, and from about 74% to about 4% in other occupations (in the occupation/country patches block)
errors.check: probe --hold typical --sweep education=11,10 --sweep occupation=6,10, with and without --set education-num=16 (linked move). Whole model with education-num 16: handlers 84.4% -> 4.5%, other 73.8% -> 3.9%, so the numbers reproduce under the whole-model scope the sentence itself names ('and the education level such people have'). Most of the drop is the direct education-num term (ann_115 -0.89 -> -4.72); through the patches (ann_119/ann_123) a doctorate moves the score by -0.39 (other) and -0.90 (handlers), about 74% -> 66%. Interaction direction holds. Part effect stated with whole-model numbers in a part block: the number reproduces under the other scope, so weakened.

errors.statement: A higher education level lowers the predicted chance of a low income in stages: about 89% at 7 to about 24% at 13, flattening out near the top
errors.check: probe --hold typical --sweep education-num=1:16:16: ann_115 falls by exactly 0.548 log-odds per level (+3.50 at 1 ... -0.89 at 9 ... -4.72 at 16), risk 89.4% at 7, 23.9% at 13. The scale is discrete, so the effect does come level by level ('in stages' read as step by step), and the same sentence describes the chance-scale flattening correctly. 'In stages' does not assert uneven steps or plateaus; not an error under the natural reading.
